'''Gisela Kaplan''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|AM|FRSN}} is an [[Australians|Australian]] [[ethologist]] who primarily specialises in [[ornithology]] and [[primatology]]. She is a [[professor emeritus]] in animal behaviour at the [[University of New England (Australia)|University of New England]], [[Australia]],<ref name="emeritus">{{Cite web|url= https://www.une.edu.au/staff-profiles/science-and-technology/gkaplan|title= Staff profile: G Kaplan|website=University of New England|accessdate=12 October 2019|date=3 February 2017}}</ref> and also honorary professor of the [[Queensland Brain Institute]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://qbi.uq.edu.au/profile/445/gisela-kaplan|title=Staff Directory – Professor Gisela Kaplan|website=Queensland Brain Institute / University of Queensland|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180415120546/https://qbi.uq.edu.au/profile/445/gisela-kaplan|archive-date=15 April 2018|accessdate=19 December 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Academic career==

Kaplan graduated from [[Monash University]] with a [[Doctor of Philosophy]].<ref name="emeritus" />

She published her first book with Clive Kessler, ''Hannah Arendt: Thinking, Judging, Freedom'' in 1989,<ref>{{Cite book|title=Hannah Arendt: Thinking, Judging, Freedom|isbn=978-0049201095|last1=Kaplan|first1=Gisela T.|last2=Kessler|first2=Clive S.|year=1989|publisher=Allen & Unwin }}</ref> followed by ''Contemporary Western European Feminism'' in 1990.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Contemporary Western European Feminism|isbn=978-0415752213 |last1=Kaplan |first1=Gisela |date=21 March 2014 |publisher=Routledge }}</ref> In 2005, she submitted a second thesis, titled ''Vocal behaviour of Australian magpies (Gymnorhina tibicen).''<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=2005 Thesis by Gisela Kaplan|url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/version/22860770|accessdate=19 December 2017|website=Trove – National Library of Australia}}</ref>

In 2011, Kaplan was awarded an [[Honorary degree|honorary]] [[Doctorate of Science]] by the University of New England.<ref>{{cite web|title=Honorary Degree Recipients since 1955 and Emeritus Professor Awardees since 1964|url=https://www.une.edu.au/about-une/governance/une-council/council-committees/media/documents/honorary-degree-recipients-since-1955-and-emeritus-professor-awardees-since-1964|accessdate=19 December 2017|website=University of New England}}</ref> In 2015, she was conferred honorary fellow of the [[American Ornithological Society]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Results of AOU Elections, 2015|url=http://ornithologyexchange.org/forums/topic/24937-results-of-aou-elections-2015/|accessdate=19 December 2017|website=Ornithology Exchange – American Ornithological Society|archive-date=22 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222053028/http://ornithologyexchange.org/forums/topic/24937-results-of-aou-elections-2015/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The following year, she was awarded the status of emeritus professor by the University of New England.<ref name="staff">{{cite web|title=Emeritus Professor Gisela Kaplan|url=http://www.une.edu.au/staff-current/une-areas/governance/une-council/council-committees/media/documents/emeritus-professor-appointments/emeritus-professor-gisela-kaplan|website=University of New England – Staff Directory|accessdate=19 December 2017}}</ref> She also received the [[Whitley Awards (Australia)|Whitley Award]] in Behavioural Zoology for her book ''Bird Minds'' in 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Whitley Awards – Commendation Awards|url=http://www.rzsnsw.org.au/commendation-page|accessdate=19 December 2017|website=Royal Zoological Society of NSW|archive-date=22 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222052828/http://www.rzsnsw.org.au/commendation-page|url-status=dead}}</ref>

She has given interviews for ABC Radio.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=8 November 2019|title=Talking magpies, grieving tawny frogmouths and canny galahs|url=https://www.abc.net.au/radio/programs/conversations/gisela-kaplan-native-birds/11665574|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=ABC|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation}}</ref>

In March 2021 Kaplan was elected Fellow of the [[Royal Society of New South Wales]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=1292nd Ordinary General Meeting|url=https://www.royalsoc.org.au/images/easyblog_docs/RSN_1292_OGM_Agenda_7_April_2021_v2.pdf|access-date=2021-08-12|website=The Royal Society of New South Wales|archive-date=12 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210812034048/https://www.royalsoc.org.au/images/easyblog_docs/RSN_1292_OGM_Agenda_7_April_2021_v2.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was appointed an Honorary [[Order of Australia|Member of the Order of Australia]] in the [[2024 Australia Day Honours]] for her "significant service to science education through research into animal behaviour".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Emeritus Professor Gisela Kaplan [H] |url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/3018012 |access-date=2024-01-25 |website=Australian Honours Search Facility}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In the 1990s, she began hand-raising and rehabilitating native birds, which she continues to do in her spare time.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://abcmedia.akamaized.net/radio/local_brisbane/audio/201911/aaj-2019-11-08.mp3|title=Talking magpies, grieving tawny frogmouths and canny galahs – Gisela Kaplan in conversation with Sarah Kanowski|date=8 November 2019|access-date=11 November 2019}}</ref>

==Publications==
Kaplan has published over 250 research articles and 23 books in total. Since 2000, she has focused on animal vocal behaviour, communication and cognition specifically in birds and primates.<ref name="emeritus" />

{{overly detailed|section|date=April 2020}}
